title: Panorra API Go New Project Report

issues.display_title: Issue #416: API: POST /users/onboarding — save personalization answers (pwa#3223)
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 30/07/26

✅ Implementation: Personalization Onboarding Save API

This document tracks the implementation of
panorra-api-new#416,
reviewed through panorra-api-new#418.

Endpoint

  • Added authenticated POST /users/onboarding.
  • Restricted access to users with role == "user"; viewer sessions receive HTTP 401.
  • Accepted partial payloads so each onboarding screen can save independently without clearing previously stored answers.
  • Kept preferences editable after onboarding completion.
  • Treated completed: false as no completion update; it does not reset completed onboarding.

Supported request fields:

{
  "discovery_source": "social_media",
  "place_interests": ["nature_scenery", "food_markets"],
  "usage_intent": "plan_trip",
  "completed": true,
  "ec": true
}

Every answer field uses a pointer in the request struct, preserving the difference between an omitted field and an explicitly supplied value.

Model

Updated src/Models/UserDetail.go with:

  • onboarding_completed
  • discovery_source
  • place_interests
  • usage_intent
  • onboarding_completed_at

Schema migration remains tracked separately in issue #417.

Validation

  • Validated discovery_source against six supported values.
  • Validated place_interests against eight supported values.
  • Deduplicated interests while preserving request order.
  • Required at least one interest when place_interests is supplied.
  • Applied no maximum interest count for v1.
  • Validated usage_intent against six supported values.
  • Rejected completed: true unless discovery source, interests, and usage intent are available from the current request or stored state.
  • Parsed stored interests as a JSON string array before checking completion. JSON null, [], and malformed JSON do not count as saved interests.
  • Stamped onboarding_completed_at server-side with time.Now().

Response Encryption

The endpoint returns the full saved onboarding state. Website requests may send "ec": true to receive the established legacy website encryption format using Functions.KeyEncrypt and Functions.EncryptResult:

{
  "cry": "<encrypted response>",
  "ls": 1785398400
}

Without ec: true, the endpoint returns the normal JSON response. The slim sl=true encryption variant is deliberately not added because this endpoint targets the website EncryptResult contract.

Routing and Documentation

  • Added SaveOnboarding controller delegation.
  • Registered POST /users/onboarding in the user route group.
  • Added Bruno collection files under api-collection/Panorra API Post/User/Onboarding/.
  • Added examples for partial saves, invalid enum rejection, and premature completion rejection.

Review Adjustments

PR #418 review produced these changes:

  • Replaced the raw JSON byte-length interest check with JSON unmarshalling and element-count validation.
  • Removed the unreachable uuid.Nil check after GORM First, because missing rows are already handled through gorm.ErrRecordNotFound.
  • Documented that completed: false does not reset onboarding.
  • Added regression coverage for stored interest JSON containing one item, an empty array, null, or malformed JSON.

Verification

The following commands passed after applying review feedback:

go test ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Status

  • Implementation and review fixes: completed locally.
  • Review fixes: not committed or pushed.
  • Merge: pending user decision.

Write side of the Personalization Onboarding flow specified in panorra-pwa#3223 (formerly named "KYC").

Nothing exists for this yet. A grep for onboard|preference|interest|kyc|personaliz across both panorra-api-new and panorra-api-go returns nothing — this is greenfield.

Related

  • Blocked by the migration — #417. The columns must exist before this ships.
  • Read side — GoThruMedia/panorra-api-go#471

Why one endpoint

The frontend spec needs three things: save answers per screen (§14 "Answers are saved before screen transition"), restore progress after refresh (§14 "return to the most recent incomplete screen"), and a completion flag so the flow does not reopen (§12).

Saving is one partial-upsert endpoint, called on every Continue — not four per-screen endpoints. Each screen sends a different field but the logic is identical. Restoring is handled by the existing GET /users/detail, covered in panorra-api-go#471.

1. Model — src/Models/UserDetail.go

Add five fields to the struct, after QueueNewPosts on line 29:

	OnboardingCompleted   bool            `gorm:"column:onboarding_completed;not null" json:"onboarding_completed"`
	DiscoverySource       *string         `gorm:"column:discovery_source" json:"discovery_source"`
	PlaceInterests        json.RawMessage `gorm:"column:place_interests" json:"place_interests"`
	UsageIntent           *string         `gorm:"column:usage_intent" json:"usage_intent"`
	OnboardingCompletedAt *time.Time      `gorm:"column:onboarding_completed_at" json:"onboarding_completed_at"`

json and time are already imported. Pointers for the nullable fields, matching the existing Language / ThemeStyle pattern.

2. New action — src/Action/V1/Users/SaveOnboarding.go

Follows the structure of UpdateRefreshTimeline.go: role guard, userId from locals, Updates(map[string]interface{}), Functions.ErrorResponse.

package Users

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"panorra-api-new/src/Config"
	"panorra-api-new/src/Models"
	"panorra-api-new/src/Utils/Functions"
	"time"

	"github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
	"github.com/google/uuid"
	"gorm.io/gorm"
)

var discoverySources = map[string]bool{
	"social_media": true, "friend_or_family": true, "search_engine": true,
	"blog_or_article": true, "event_or_community": true, "other": true,
}

var placeInterestOptions = map[string]bool{
	"attractions": true, "nature_scenery": true, "history_heritage": true,
	"culture_local_life": true, "food_markets": true, "hotels_stays": true,
	"events_venues": true, "architecture_unique_places": true,
}

var usageIntents = map[string]bool{
	"explore_virtually": true, "find_near_me": true, "plan_trip": true,
	"discover_hidden_gems": true, "preview_venue_property": true, "upload_share_360": true,
}

type onboardingRequest struct {
	DiscoverySource *string   `json:"discovery_source"`
	PlaceInterests  *[]string `json:"place_interests"`
	UsageIntent     *string   `json:"usage_intent"`
	Completed       *bool     `json:"completed"`
}

func SaveOnboarding(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
	if c.Locals("role").(string) != "user" {
		return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 401, fiber.ErrUnauthorized.Message, "Unauthorized")
	}

	userId := c.Locals("userId").(string)

	var req onboardingRequest
	if err := c.BodyParser(&req); err != nil {
		return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 400, fiber.ErrBadRequest.Message, "Invalid Body")
	}

	var userDetail Models.UserDetail
	if err := Config.DB.Model(&Models.UserDetail{}).
		Select("id, discovery_source, place_interests, usage_intent").
		Where("user_id = ?", userId).
		First(&userDetail).Error; err != nil {
		if err == gorm.ErrRecordNotFound {
			return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 409, fiber.ErrConflict.Message, "User Not Found")
		}
		return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 500, fiber.ErrInternalServerError.Message, "Internal Server Error")
	}

	if userDetail.ID == uuid.Nil {
		return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 409, fiber.ErrConflict.Message, "User Not Found")
	}

	updates := map[string]interface{}{}

	if req.DiscoverySource != nil {
		if !discoverySources[*req.DiscoverySource] {
			return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 422, fiber.ErrUnprocessableEntity.Message, "Invalid Discovery Source", "discovery_source")
		}
		updates["discovery_source"] = *req.DiscoverySource
	}

	if req.PlaceInterests != nil {
		seen := map[string]bool{}
		unique := make([]string, 0, len(*req.PlaceInterests))
		for _, v := range *req.PlaceInterests {
			if !placeInterestOptions[v] {
				return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 422, fiber.ErrUnprocessableEntity.Message, "Invalid Place Interest", "place_interests")
			}
			if !seen[v] {
				seen[v] = true
				unique = append(unique, v)
			}
		}
		if len(unique) == 0 {
			return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 422, fiber.ErrUnprocessableEntity.Message, "Required at least one place interest", "place_interests")
		}
		raw, _ := json.Marshal(unique)
		updates["place_interests"] = json.RawMessage(raw)
	}

	if req.UsageIntent != nil {
		if !usageIntents[*req.UsageIntent] {
			return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 422, fiber.ErrUnprocessableEntity.Message, "Invalid Usage Intent", "usage_intent")
		}
		updates["usage_intent"] = *req.UsageIntent
	}

	if req.Completed != nil && *req.Completed {
		hasSource := updates["discovery_source"] != nil ||
			(userDetail.DiscoverySource != nil && *userDetail.DiscoverySource != "")
		hasInterests := updates["place_interests"] != nil || len(userDetail.PlaceInterests) > 2 // "[]" is 2 bytes
		hasIntent := updates["usage_intent"] != nil ||
			(userDetail.UsageIntent != nil && *userDetail.UsageIntent != "")

		if !hasSource || !hasInterests || !hasIntent {
			return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 422, fiber.ErrUnprocessableEntity.Message, "Incomplete Onboarding", "completed")
		}

		updates["onboarding_completed"] = true
		updates["onboarding_completed_at"] = time.Now()
	}

	if len(updates) == 0 {
		return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 400, fiber.ErrBadRequest.Message, "Required Input Body", "Nothing to save")
	}

	if err := Config.DB.Model(&Models.UserDetail{}).
		Where("id = ?", userDetail.ID).
		Updates(updates).Error; err != nil {
		return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 500, fiber.ErrInternalServerError.Message, "Internal Server Error")
	}

	var saved Models.UserDetail
	if err := Config.DB.Model(&Models.UserDetail{}).
		Select("onboarding_completed, discovery_source, place_interests, usage_intent, onboarding_completed_at").
		Where("id = ?", userDetail.ID).
		First(&saved).Error; err != nil {
		return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 500, fiber.ErrInternalServerError.Message, "Internal Server Error")
	}

	return c.Status(fiber.StatusOK).JSON(fiber.Map{
		"statusCode": 200,
		"data": fiber.Map{
			"valid":    true,
			"messages": "Success Save Onboarding",
			"onboarding": fiber.Map{
				"completed":        saved.OnboardingCompleted,
				"discovery_source": saved.DiscoverySource,
				"place_interests":  saved.PlaceInterests,
				"usage_intent":     saved.UsageIntent,
				"completed_at":     saved.OnboardingCompletedAt,
			},
		},
	})
}

Design notes

Every request field is a pointer so "field not sent" is distinguishable from "sent empty". Screen 1 sends only discovery_source, screen 2 only place_interests. Without pointers, Updates would overwrite the previous screen's answer with an empty string.

The row is read before the update because the completed gate (§16 Screen 4, "All previous answers must be successfully saved") needs to know what is already stored, not just what this request carries.

The role != "user" guard matters. The viewer role passes the auth middleware with an empty userId (AuthMiddleware.go:94-96). Without the guard, Where("user_id = ?", "") either errors or matches an arbitrary row.

onboarding_completed_at is stamped server-side, never taken from the client.

The response returns full state so the frontend does not need a follow-up GET after each save.

All enums are validated server-side. The frontend owns the copy, icons and descriptions; the API owns the accepted values. There is deliberately no endpoint serving the option list — the enums are static in the spec, and an extra round trip in front of the first screen buys nothing.

Enum values (spec §15)

discovery_source:  social_media | friend_or_family | search_engine |
                   blog_or_article | event_or_community | other

place_interests:   attractions | nature_scenery | history_heritage |
                   culture_local_life | food_markets | hotels_stays |
                   events_venues | architecture_unique_places

usage_intent:      explore_virtually | find_near_me | plan_trip |
                   discover_hidden_gems | preview_venue_property | upload_share_360

3. Controller — src/Controllers/V1/UsersController.go

func SaveOnboarding(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
	return UsersAction.SaveOnboarding(c)
}

4. Route — src/Routes/V1/UsersRoutes.go

Add to the User group, around line 31:

	User.Post("/onboarding", Controllers.SaveOnboarding)

Auth is automatic — the middleware is registered globally at Client.go:46, not per route.

5. Bruno collection

New folder api-collection/Panorra API Post/User/Onboarding/ with folder.yml and Save Onboarding.yml. Follow the format of Contact Us.yml, but with body.type: json.

Worth covering: each screen's partial save, a rejected enum value, and completed: true sent before all three answers exist.

6. Tests

This repo currently has zero _test.go files, so anything added here is the first.

The enum validation and the completed gate are pure functions and the easiest part of this to get subtly wrong — a SaveOnboarding_test.go covering the three enum tables and the gate's combinations would be cheap. Team call, given it sets a precedent.

Acceptance criteria

  • Models.UserDetail has the five new fields
  • POST /users/onboarding accepts partial payloads without clobbering previously saved answers
  • discovery_source validated against the six values above
  • place_interests validated against the eight values above, deduplicated, at least one required
  • usage_intent validated against the six values above
  • completed: true rejected with 422 unless all three answers are present
  • onboarding_completed_at set server-side, never from the client
  • viewer role rejected with 401
  • Response returns the full onboarding state after save
  • Bruno collection added

Open questions

  1. Maximum for place_interests? §16 says unrestricted for the initial version with an "optional future limit: maximum five". Decide now — retrofitting a limit after users have saved more than five is worse than setting it up front.
  2. Does reopening from Profile → Preferences (§25) land in v1? The code above allows re-saving after completed: true. If it should lock, that needs a guard.

Out of scope

Reading the state back is panorra-api-go#471. The migration is #417. The four screens, progress bar, keyboard navigation and accessibility work are frontend, tracked in panorra-pwa#3223. The analytics events in §21 are frontend telemetry, not an API surface. §24 of the spec rules out identity verification, document upload and facial verification entirely — despite the original "KYC" name, none of that is being built.
